findings.title: Stored XSS via unescaped URL and unsanitized raw_html
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, TopicEmbed.import interpolates the attacker-controlled url directly into HTML: "#{url}" with only a /^https?:\/\// prefix check. A URL like http://embeddable_host/'> passes the check and has the allowed host, so TopicRetriever will accept it. The resulting HTML is stored as a Post with cook_method raw_html (line 22) which bypasses all cooking/sanitization in Post#cook, and rendered with raw post.cooked in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19. Consequence is persistent stored XSS executed in browsers viewing the embed or topic.

findings.title: Nil feed content crashes entire poll
findings.body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35, poll_feed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). RSS 2.0 items often have no content element (only description/title) and SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content. Calling scrub on nil raises NoMethodError with no rescue, aborting the loop. Consequence is one legacy item prevents all feed items from being imported/updated and fails the hourly scheduled job.

findings.title: Unsafe open of feed URL with no error handling
findings.body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, code does SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) using Kernel#open/open-uri on an admin setting with no URI validation, timeout, or rescue. It allows file:// or pipe arguments in older Ruby, follows redirects arbitrarily (SSRF), and any network/DNS/parse error raises out of the scheduled job. Consequence is job failure, Sidekiq noise, and potential local-file read or internal-network fetch.

findings.title: import_remote uses open without require or rescue
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, import_remote does open(url).read without requiring open-uri in that file and without begin/rescue/timeout/validation. If open-uri was not already loaded it does local file open, and any 404/timeout/invalid URL raises. Called from TopicRetriever.fetch_http and Disqus import, the exception bubbles and fails the RetrieveTopic job. Consequence is embed retrieval never completes and repeated retries on every embed view.

findings.title: Mutates caller string with <<
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, import does contents << "\n<hr>..." which mutates the caller's String in place instead of duping. If the caller reuses the string it gets a second footer on retry, and frozen strings raise RuntimeError. Consequence is duplicated imported-from footers, surprising side effects, and crashes with frozen literals.

findings.title: No handling for missing/deleted embed post
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 32, the update path does post = embed.post then PostRevisor.new(post).revise! with no nil check. If the post/topic was deleted, trashed, or never created due to failed PostCreator, post is nil and revise! raises NoMethodError. There is also no check that revise! succeeded before embed.update_column(:content_sha1). Consequence is poll/retrieve jobs crash mid-loop and sha can diverge from actual post content.

findings.title: downcase on possibly nil embed_by_username
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49, fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase with no blank check. If the setting is nil (default/unset in tests and fresh installs) this raises NoMethodError. Unlike PollFeed#execute which guards present?, every embed retrieval via RetrieveTopic hits this. Consequence is all embed fetches raise instead of no-op until admin configures the user.

findings.title: Non-atomic throttle with raw URL as Redis key
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 27, retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(key,1) then separate $redis.expire(key,60). If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. The key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" using unbounded user input, allowing huge keys and memory abuse. Consequence is permanent denial of retrieval for a URL and Redis bloat; should use SET NX EX atomically and hash the URL.

findings.title: postMessage origin check is reversed
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17, the check is discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1, i.e. does discourseUrl contain e.origin, instead of checking e.origin equals the Discourse origin. Any origin that is a prefix/substring passes, e.g. discourseUrl http://example.com contains attacker origin http://example.co. Consequence is a malicious page can send discourse-resize messages to control iframe height, and the pattern invites broader message forgery if more types are added.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer
findings.body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>') where request.referer is the full URL including path/query, not an origin. The postMessage spec requires scheme+host+port; passing a full URL means the message is never delivered (or throws). When referer is nil it passes empty string which throws. Consequence is embed auto-resize is broken and relies on attacker-controlled header for security boundary.

findings.title: absolutize_urls raises on malformed URL
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 57, absolutize_urls does URI(url) with no rescue. Any malformed embed_url or feed link raises URI::InvalidURIError and aborts import/revise and the calling job. It also only handles href/src starting with / and mishandles protocol-relative //host/path, leaving broken or wrong absolute URLs. Consequence is single bad URL fails feed poll or embed retrieval.

findings.title: Disqus replies pass ignored cooked param
findings.body: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor line 160, the importer builds attrs with raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked]. PostCreator.setup_post only reads raw and computes cooked via Post#cook; the cooked key is ignored. First post is created as raw_html via TopicEmbed.import_remote but replies are created as regular markdown posts containing raw HTML. Consequence is Disqus HTML is escaped/sanitized inconsistently, breaking formatting and losing intended rendering.

findings.title: Spec mocks TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
findings.body: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb line 40, the test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly, while app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15 does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). If test jobs run inline the mock may accidentally pass, otherwise it fails, and in production the async path with user_id/embed_url args, throttling, and host validation is never asserted. Consequence is the real enqueue contract is untested and regressions will not be caught.
